newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Monopoly champ eyes world title.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Monopoly champ eyes world title.

text.p: For more than two decades the world championship in Monopoly, the U.S.-invented board game of raw capitalism, power and chance, has been captured by players from outside the United States.

But Roger Craig, a 35-year-old tire salesman from Harrisburg, Illinois, said on Monday he has a good chance to change that. Craig, the reigning U.S. Monopoly champion, will compete in Monte Carlo next weekend against champions from more than 35 countries as he seeks to wrest the title from Joost Van Orten of the Netherlands.
The world championship has not been won by someone from the United States since 1975.

"I feel pretty confident," said Craig, who got hooked on the board game as a child visiting his grandmother. He started playing in earnest in 1987, winning a local competition, and last year in New York City he snagged the national Monopoly championship.

Now he faces four 90-minute preliminary rounds over the first two days of competition followed by a faceoff among four finalists in an untimed game. The winner, who must bankrupt all opponents and seize control of the board, will collect $15,140 -- the amount of money in a Monopoly game.

Monopoly, which combines the power of property ownership with risk at each roll of the dice, is manufactured by Parker Brothers in Beverly, Massachusetts., a division of Hasbro Inc. Since 1935, the game has sold more than 160 million copies and is available in 26 languages in over 75 countries.
Craig told Reuters his strategy lay in buying the right properties and being well versed in all the rules.
"Win, lose or draw, this is the trip of a lifetime," added Craig, who has never travelled outside the United States.
